title: POC scoping - Integration planning with Astor Analytics
summary: Redwood AE/SE and Astor team scoped POC integration: targets are OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDK integration, function/tool calling for retrieval and structured JSON outputs. Success criteria include latency < 350ms p50 for short completions, 95% structured output validity, and cost per 1k requests target. Security checks (SOC2, KMS) and timeline for a 4-week pilot agreed.
topics: integration options: SDK vs HTTP/compat endpoint
function/tool calling and structured output schema
next_steps: Redwood: send POC runbook + sample benchmark scripts (Liam) by 2026-10-09
Astor: provide representative prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-10-10
Schedule technical kickoff and baseline benchmark run week of 2026-10-12
action_items: Liam O'Connor - share SDK quickstart repo and sample code (node/python) - 2026-10-09
Jordan Blake - export 2 weeks of traffic profile and 200 sample prompts - 2026-10-10
Elena Park - confirm required compliance docs and KMS policy questions - 2026-10-12
Maya Chen - send pricing and pilot SOW draft - 2026-10-11
transcript: Header: 2026-10-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM); Jordan Blake (Astor CTO), Priya Nair (Eng Manager), Diego Ramos (ML Eng), Elena Park (Security)
Links shared: Redwood POC runbook (link), SDK quickstart repo (github.com/redwood/quickstart), benchmark spreadsheet (sheets.google.com/astor-bench), security pack (redwood.com/sec/soc2.pdf)
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda - scope success criteria, integration approach (sdk vs http), function calling needs, and timeline. Jordan you on mute?

[00:18] Jordan (Astor, CTO): yeah sorry, can hear you. main goal for us is to integrate LLM-driven insights into our client dashboard. we want reliable structured JSON output for entity extraction and action suggestions. low latency is important for interactive flows.

[01:05] Priya (Astor): and also want to keep costs predictable - we run about 350k inference events/month currently in batch and expect spikes on demo days. trying to understand how Redwood's dedicated vs hosted will play in the POC.
[01:40] Liam (Redwood SE): great, thanks. quick clarification: for structured output you want a strict schema? or tolerant/heuristic parsing?
[01:55] Diego (Astor): strict schema. 95% validity on returned JSON fields is our bar, otherwise we need fallback human review - not acceptable for production flow.

[02:20] Maya: okay success criteria note: 1) Structured output validity >= 95% on our sample prompts; 2) p50 latency for short completions < 350ms on hosted endpoint or with dedicated pool; 3) cost target - roughly $X per 1k requests (we'll calc after initial bench). also security: SOC2+, KMS for key control, and audit logs.
[03:05] Elena (Astor, Security): on KMS: we need customer-managed keys and audit trails, and some clarity on data residency. can you outline options for Private or VPC deployments for the pilot?

[03:30] Ravi (Redwood CSM): we can run pilot on Hosted with VPC peering or a Private deployment depending on your compliance needs. for initial bench we often use OpenAI-compatible endpoints in Hosted mode to simplify integration, then move to Dedicated if throughput/latency requires it.
[04:02] Priya: curious - the SDKs, is there parity between SDK and the OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints? we prefer to use your node SDK inside our backend for retries and instrumentation.

[04:25] Liam: yes SDKs are thin wrappers around the OpenAI-compatible API but include helpers for structured output validation, streaming handling, and built-in retries. we'll share node and python samples that show function calling and structured output validators.

[05:10] Diego: function calling - we need to call our retrieval tool, pass a document context, and get back JSON with fields: intent, entities[]. start_token and end_token positions. does Redwood support tool calling patterns or the 'function call' spec?

[05:35] Liam: we support OpenAI-compatible function calling patterns; we also have an 'invoke-tool' extension to route calls to external services. small caveat: sometimes transcriptions show product names differently but runtime supports name-mapped tools. for the POC we can mock the retrieval service and run an end-to-end test.

[06:20] Jordan: great. on workload sizing - our current peak qps is around 40 qps with spikes to 120 for short windows. median request size is small (50-120 tokens) but we have some long-form summarizations too. can you recommend batching or KV cache config?

[06:52] Liam: for interactive low-latency flows avoid large batching. KV cache/prefix caching helps long multi-step dialogs - recommend enabling prefix cache for sessioned flows and set batching window small (10-20ms) to keep latency low. if you need heavy throughput, Dedicated pool with continuous batching is best.
[07:25] Priya: benchmark methodology? we'll need baseline numbers to compare. what exact metrics should we run?

[07:40] Maya: benchmark spreadsheet will list tests - single-shot latency p50/p95, structured output correctness run on 200 sample prompts, throughput saturation tests, and error-rate under load. we like to run both hosted and a dedicated-config baseline if threshold indicates.
[08:10] Diego: how do we wire retries so we don't double-charge for tokens? we have strict cost accounting.

[08:28] Liam: SDK exposes idempotency keys and at-most-once helpers. plus Redwood metrics include token-level cost breakdown so you can reconcile. we'll include sample instrumentation in the quickstart repo.
[09:00] Elena: compliance question - will we get audit logs that show request/response metadata but not full PII? we need redaction controls.
[09:18] Ravi: yes audit logs available; we also support automatic redaction hooks and customer-managed PII scrubbing before ingestion. more details in the security pack link shared earlier.
[10:05] Jordan: timeline - ideally pilot run in 4 weeks, start integration this week, baseline bench in week 2, iterate and have pilot sign-off end of week 4. is that realistic?

[10:30] Maya: yes that's typical. propose: this week - exchange prompts and runbook; week 2 - baseline benchmark (hosted); week 3 - tune and run second benchmark with SDK and function calls; week 4 - final results and SOW for next phase.
[11:02] Priya: any blockers on our side? we need sample code for function call wiring and structured schema enforcement - can you send validators?

[11:18] Liam: we'll share a schema validator snippet that asserts required fields and returns structured parse scores. also include a streaming example for interactive UI so you can render partial JSON safely.
[12:00] Diego: question about model variants - does Redwood automatically fallback to quantized or cheaper variants? we worry about quality regressions.

[12:20] Maya: smart routing can fallback to compatible variants by policy; for POC we'll pin to a specific model to avoid regressions. Optimize tooling can recommend quantization once you pass quality gates.
[13:05] Jordan: competitor question - do you have any direct customers using similar flow? we evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic protos - curious on cost/latency delta.

[13:30] Maya: yes we have finance and search customers with similar flows; we'll share anonymized benchmark comparisons. generally Dedicated gives better tail latency than public hosted endpoints at scale.
[14:00] Elena: last security ask - SSO/SAML integration for the console and RBAC for runbook access?
[14:18] Ravi: supported - we'll send the admin doc. RBAC and SSO setup can be done during pilot if needed.

[14:45] Maya: recap of next steps: Redwood sends runbook + SDK samples + initial bench scripts (Liam); Astor provides prompts and traffic profile (Jordan); Security docs follow-up (Ravi/Elena). we'll schedule the kickoff for Monday 2026-10-12 14:00 UTC.
[15:10] Jordan: thanks all, excited to get started. one last note - we want explicit criteria for structured output scoring; can you include the scoring script?
[15:28] Liam: yes will include a scorer that computes field-level precision/recall and overall validity percent. check the quickstart repo link.
[15:50] Maya: great, we'll follow up in email with links and proposed calendar invite. thanks everyone.
